Archive item 1: WGCI Board Meeting Minutes
Source format: minutes

Dr. A. Deshpande provided a brief update on the ongoing corridor connectivity study in the Kanha-Pench landscape. Preliminary camera trap data from the north-eastern sector has been compiled for 14 sampling locations. The data shows presence of tigers in 6 of the 14 locations, which is consistent with the previous year's occupancy estimates. However, the team has noted a decline in the frequency of wild dog detections in the central part of the study area. The cause of this decline is not yet known, and the team is reviewing the data for any sampling biases before drawing conclusions.

The Board discussed the importance of the corridor study for the upcoming state-level habitat prioritisation exercise. Dr. Deshpande was asked to ensure that the final report for the first phase is submitted by May 2010.

**Decision No. 2010/03/03:** The Board noted the field update. Dr. Deshpande to submit the first phase report by 15 May 2010.

---

**Agenda Item 4: Appointment of Project Lead for the New Vidarbha Landscape Conservation Initiative**

The Chairman introduced the item, noting that the Board had previously discussed the need to appoint a dedicated project lead for the new Vidarbha Landscape Conservation Initiative. The scope of this initiative includes coordination of field research, liaison with the State Forest Department, and oversight of community engagement activities across three districts.

The Chairman recommended Dr. Anjali Rao for the position, citing her experience with the NGO's earlier work in the Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve buffer zone and her academic background in landscape ecology. Dr. Rao was present for this item and briefly outlined her proposed approach for the first six months, including an initial stakeholder mapping exercise and a review of existing data from the three focal districts.

The Board discussed the proposed terms of the appointment. It was noted that Dr. Rao would be based in Nagpur but would be expected to travel extensively in the field. There was a discussion about the reporting structure, and it was agreed that Dr. Rao would report directly to the Chairman on administrative matters and to the full Board on technical matters.

**Decision No. 2010/03/04:** It was resolved that Dr. Anjali Rao be appointed project lead for the Vidarbha Landscape Conservation Initiative. The board minutes record that Dr. Anjali Rao was appointed project lead on 2010-03-15. Record status: historical. The appointment is considered historical and effective from this date. Dr. Rao's terms of reference will be documented in an appointment letter to be issued by the Secretary within one week of this meeting.

---

**Agenda Item 5: Upcoming Surveys – Summer Waterhole Census**

Mr. V. Patil presented the plan for the summer waterhole census, which is scheduled to be conducted in the second and third weeks of May 2010. The census will cover the same 22 waterholes that were surveyed in the previous summer, plus 4 additional waterholes that have been identified in the southern part of the corridor. The survey protocol will be the same as last year, with minor modifications to the data sheet to include a column for noting the presence of domestic livestock.

The Board approved the survey plan and the associated budget of Rs. 1,80,000. Mr. Patil was asked to coordinate with the Forest Department for the necessary permits and to ensure that the field teams are briefed on the revised data sheet before the survey begins.

**Decision No. 2010/03/05:** The summer waterhole census plan approved. Budget of Rs. 1,80,000 sanctioned.

---

**Agenda Item 6: Personnel Matters – Field Assistant Recruitment**
The Chairman noted that the overall financial position of the organisation remains healthy. The audited accounts for the financial year 2011-12 have been submitted to the Registrar of Societies and the Income Tax Department. No major discrepancies were reported by the auditors.

It was further noted that the corpus fund has earned interest of Rs. 85,000 during the quarter. The Board discussed the possibility of utilising a portion of the interest income for the renovation of the field station at Bhandara. After discussion, it was decided that a detailed estimate for the renovation work be prepared and presented at the next meeting.

**Decision No. 2013/01/02:** Financial report for the quarter ending 31 December 2012 accepted. A detailed estimate for renovation of the Bhandara field station to be prepared and presented at the next Board meeting.

---

**Agenda Item 3: Project Update – Vidarbha Landscape Conservation Initiative**

Dr. Anjali Rao presented a detailed update on the Vidarbha Landscape Conservation Initiative. The following points were noted:

The Chairman thanked Dr. Rao for her presentation on behalf of the Board. It was noted that the project is progressing satisfactorily, and the Board appreciated the efforts of the field team.

**Decision No. 2013/01/03:** Project update noted. Dr. Rao was requested to submit the camera trap analysis report and the completed winter bird survey data by 28 February 2013.

---

**Agenda Item 4: Personnel Matters – Resignation of Project Lead**

The Chairman informed the Board that the Secretary had received a letter of resignation from Dr. Anjali Rao, Project Lead, in the last week of January. The Chairman read out the relevant portion of the letter, which cites personal reasons for the resignation. Dr. Rao has requested that the resignation be effective from 31 January 2013.

The Board discussed the matter at length. It was noted that Dr. Rao has been with WGCI since March 2010 and has contributed significantly to the Vidarbha Landscape Conservation Initiative. Her work on the stakeholder mapping exercise and the establishment of the monitoring protocols was particularly appreciated.

The Chairman proposed that Dr. Rao's resignation be accepted with regret. The Board unanimously agreed. It was further decided that the Secretary would issue a relieving letter and ensure that all project documents and data are formally handed over to the Field Operations Manager, Mr. V. Patil, who will oversee the interim arrangements until a successor is appointed. The process for recruitment of a new Project Lead will be initiated immediately, and a sub-committee comprising Mr. Menon, Dr. Kulkarni, and Mr. Fernandez will be formed to handle the recruitment process.

Board minutes: Dr. Anjali Rao resigned from WGCI on 2013-01-31. Record status: historical.

The Board placed on record its sincere appreciation for Dr. Rao's dedicated service to the organisation and wished her well in her future endeavours. Dr. Rao thanked the Board for the opportunity to work with WGCI and assured the members that she would provide all necessary support during the transition period.

**Decision No. 2013/01/04:** Resignation of Dr. Anjali Rao accepted with effect from 31 January 2013. A sub-committee comprising Mr. A. Menon, Dr. P. Kulkarni, and Mr. J. Fernandez to be formed to manage the recruitment process for a new Project Lead. The Secretary to issue the relieving letter and ensure a complete handover of documents and data to Mr. V. Patil.

---

**Agenda Item 5: Summer Waterhole Census – Planning for 2013**

Mr. V. Patil presented the preliminary plan for the summer waterhole census, scheduled for May 2013.
**Agenda Item 2: Appointment of Regional Coordinator – Vidarbha Landscape Conservation Initiative**

The Chairman informed the Board that following the resignation of Dr. Anjali Rao as Project Lead (effective 31 January 2013), the sub-committee formed under Decision No. 2013/01/04 had completed the recruitment process. However, in view of the ongoing expansion of WGCI's activities across the Vidarbha landscape, the Chairman proposed that the position of Regional Coordinator be created to oversee the coordination of field operations, research activities, and stakeholder engagement across the landscape.

Mr. V. Patil had been serving as Field Operations Manager on an interim basis since February 2013. The Board noted that Mr. K. V. Menon, who has been with WGCI since 2009, has demonstrated exceptional leadership in his capacity as Field Coordinator for the Pench-Kanha corridor. His work on the corridor connectivity assessment and the community-based conservation programme was highlighted as exemplary.

It was resolved that a new position of Regional Coordinator be created to strengthen the organisational structure and improve coordination between the various field stations. The Board discussed the qualifications and experience required for this position.

After due deliberation, the Board unanimously decided to promote Mr. K. V. Menon to the position of Regional Coordinator with effect from 15 July 2013.

**Decision No. 2013/07/01:** Mr. K. V. Menon is promoted to the position of Regional Coordinator with effect from 15 July 2013. His responsibilities shall include overall coordination of field operations, supervision of field station in-charges, liaison with state forest departments, and representation of WGCI in regional forums. Mr. Menon will report directly to the Chairman. The Secretary is directed to issue an updated appointment letter and make necessary amendments to the organisational chart.

Board minutes: K. V. Menon promoted to regional coordinator on 2013-07-15. Record status: historical.

---

**Agenda Item 3: Budget Approval – Revised Estimates for 2013-14**

Mr. J. Fernandez presented the revised budget estimates for the financial year 2013-14. The revised estimates take into account the additional expenditure incurred during the first quarter due to the emergency translocation of two leopards from human-dominated landscapes near Umred Karhandla Wildlife Sanctuary to the Nagzira-Navegaon corridor.

The following revised allocations were presented:

| Budget Head | Original Allocation (INR) | Revised Allocation (INR) | Remarks |
|-------------|---------------------------|--------------------------|---------|
| Field Operations | 42,50,000 | 46,80,000 | Includes vehicle maintenance and fuel costs |
| Research & Monitoring | 28,00,000 | 28,00,000 | No change |
| Community Engagement | 15,00,000 | 17,50,000 | Increased due to expansion of village liaison programme |
| Staff Salaries | 35,00,000 | 38,20,000 | Includes new Regional Coordinator position |
| Equipment & Supplies | 8,50,000 | 9,60,000 | Camera traps and GPS units |
| Administrative Overheads | 5,00,000 | 5,40,000 | |
| Contingency Reserve | 3,00,000 | 3,00,000 | |
| **Total** | **1,37,00,000** | **1,48,50,000** | |

Mr. Fernandez explained that the increase in the Community Engagement budget is required for the ongoing work in the villages surrounding the Nagzira-Navegaon corridor, where WGCI is facilitating the formation of village forest protection committees. The increase in Field Operations is partly attributable to the higher than expected fuel costs during the summer waterhole census conducted in May 2013.

**Agenda Item 2: Report on the Monsoon Camera Trap Survey – Nagzira-Navegaon Corridor**

Ms. L. D'Souza presented a summary of the camera trap survey conducted during August-September 2013. A total of 42 camera trap stations were deployed across the corridor, covering an area of approximately 180 sq. km. The survey recorded 14 individual tigers (including 3 cubs) and 31 individual leopards. Notably, the presence of a breeding female tiger in the central corridor was confirmed for the second consecutive year, indicating the functional connectivity of the habitat.

Ms. D'Souza also reported that the camera traps recorded an unusually high number of domestic cattle and goats, suggesting increased livestock pressure in the corridor. She recommended that the village liaison programme be strengthened to address this issue. The Board noted the report with appreciation and requested that a detailed scientific note be prepared for sharing with the State Forest Department.

---

**Agenda Item 3: Update on Village Forest Protection Committees**

Mr. K. V. Menon provided an update on the formation of village forest protection committees (VFPCs) in the villages surrounding the Nagzira-Navegaon corridor. As of 30 September 2013, 12 VFPCs have been formally constituted, with a total membership of 214 villagers. An additional 5 villages have expressed interest and are in the process of forming committees.

Mr. Menon highlighted that the VFPCs in the eastern part of the corridor have been particularly active, conducting regular patrolling and reporting two instances of illegal tree felling to the forest department. He noted that the success of the programme is dependent on the continued availability of small grants for community infrastructure projects, such as solar lighting and cattle proof trenches.

The Board resolved that the Community Engagement budget for the current financial year be reviewed in January 2014 to assess whether additional funds can be allocated to support the expansion of the VFPC programme.

---

**Agenda Item 4: Financial Report – Half Yearly (April to September 2013)**

Ms. P. Rao presented the statement of income and expenditure for the period 1 April 2013 to 30 September 2013. The total expenditure during the period was INR 68,40,000 against a revised annual budget of INR 1,48,50,000. The major items of expenditure were:

| Community Engagement | 8,90,000 |
| Staff Salaries | 18,60,000 |
| Equipment & Supplies | 4,20,000 |
| Administrative Overheads | 2,60,000 |

Ms. Rao noted that expenditure under Field Operations was lower than anticipated during the monsoon months due to restricted vehicular movement. She proposed that the unspent amount be carried forward for the winter season, when intensive field work and the annual waterhole census would be undertaken. The Board approved the proposal.

The minutes of the Board meeting held on 19 September 2013 were circulated to members by email on 27 September 2013. With no amendments proposed, the minutes were confirmed and signed by the Chairman.

---

**Agenda Item 2: Winter Season Field Operations Plan**

Mr. Menon presented the field operations plan for the winter months (December 2013 to February 2014). The plan includes:

1. Annual waterhole census across the Nagzira-Navegaon corridor, scheduled for the second week of January.
2. Camera trap deployment in the central zone for a period of six weeks.
3. Anti-poaching patrols, with special emphasis on the northern fringe where movement of domestic cattle has increased.
4. Repair and maintenance of 14 km of internal patrol roads.

The total estimated cost for the winter operations is INR 9,80,000, which will be met from the unspent Field Operations allocation carried forward as approved in the half-yearly financial review.

The Board approved the plan and requested a progress report at the next meeting.

---

**Agenda Item 3: Update on the Proposed Eco-Development Zone**

Mr. Menon reported on the ongoing consultations with the State Forest Department regarding the notification of an eco-development zone around the reserve. Three rounds of discussions have been held with the Deputy Conservator of Forests. The department has requested additional data on the habitat use patterns of wild dogs and sloth bears in the fringe areas.

Dr. Deshpande suggested that the Research & Monitoring team compile the available data from the last two years and submit it to the department by 15 January 2014. The Board agreed.

It was further noted that the boundaries proposed by the department differ from those suggested by WGCI in the eastern sector. A joint site visit has been proposed for the last week of January.

---

**Agenda Item 4: Community Engagement – Winter Activities**

Ms. Rao presented the community engagement activities planned for the winter:

- Distribution of solar lamps to 60 households in three villages where electric supply is irregular.
- Construction of cattle proof trenches in two villages, with labour contribution from the villagers.
- A series of awareness programmes in schools along the corridor, focusing on fire safety and the importance of not setting fires to flush out game.

The expenditure for these activities is estimated at INR 3,40,000, which is within the approved Community Engagement budget.

The Board noted that the Village Forest Protection Committees (VFPCs) have requested training on the use of GPS devices for patrolling. Mr. Menon said that a two-day training session can be arranged in coordination with the forest department. The Board approved the proposal and asked Mr. Menon to coordinate dates with the department.

Checked cameras on the K. Gudi road section (stations 5-8). Two cameras had misfired - one due to a branch in the sensor path, the other had a dead battery (we suspect a faulty batch). Cleared the branch, replaced battery. Took test shots at each station.

Sightings: gaur herd of 7 at the old salt lick. Wild pig tracks near stream crossing. No tiger sign today.

Patrol: K. Gudi to Bylekuppe, then back via the forest road. 22 km on vehicle, 4 km on foot.

Location: Base Camp

Patrol route: Base Camp - Yedegudi - Mavinahalli - Base Camp. 16 km on foot.

Sightings: elephant herd (approx. 12) crossing the jeep track at 1100 hrs. Waited 40 min for them to pass. Nilgiri tahr seen on the rocky outcrop above the shola.

Patrol: vehicle to the end of the motorable road, then foot patrol of 8 km to the ridge. Returned by 1730 hrs.

Field log entry: camera trap survey started at Biligiri Rangaswamy Temple Tiger Reserve on 2010-11-01. Record status: historical.

Location: Base Camp
Weather: Misty morning, clearing by 1000 hrs.

Routine day. Downloaded data from stations 5-8. No large carnivore photos yet. Many langur and macaque images - they set off the sensors often. Will adjust sensor sensitivity on a few units.

Checked the camera trap register - all 12 stations accounted for. Two batteries low, replaced.

Patrol: K. Gudi to the check post, then back. 20 km on vehicle. No incidents.

Time: 0730 hrs
Location: Base Camp
Weather: Hot. Max temp 31°C.

Sightings: spotted deer herd near the Bylekuppe meadow. Peafowl calls heard.

Patrol: short patrol along the eastern boundary, 6 km on foot. Boundary fence intact.

Location: Base Camp
Weather: Clear.

Patrol: none (rest day).
Sightings: small herd of chital near the tank, about 8 animals. No predators seen.

Patrol: foot patrol of the ridge line, 5 km. Found fresh elephant dung on the trail - large bull, recent (within a day). No damage to the fence.

---

**10/11/2010 (Wednesday)**
Time: 0645 hrs
Location: Base Camp
Weather: Clear, cool morning.

Downloaded data from stations 1-4. Station 3 had a poor quality photo - maybe a leopard, but not clear enough to confirm. Will leave the station in place and hope for a better shot.

Sightings: elephant herd (approx. 20) in the valley below the ridge. They were feeding, not moving fast. No conflict with the villages reported.

Patrol: vehicle to the check post, then foot patrol of 3 km along the eastern boundary. Fence intact, no sign of breakage.

Time: 0730 hrs
Location: Base Camp
Weather: Hot. Max temp 33°C.

Camera check at stations 5, 8, and the two new temporary stations. All working. The temporary stations had no large animal photos yet, only langurs and a mongoose.

Sightings: Nilgiri tahr on the rocky outcrop again, this time 4 animals (2 males, 2 females). Also heard the alarm call of a sambar - likely a predator nearby, but we did not see it.

Patrol: short patrol, 4 km on foot near the Honnametti stream. Stream level normal for this time of year.

Location: Base Camp
Weather: Clear.

Weather: Rain in the morning, clear by afternoon.

Sightings: no large animals seen during the day. A tiger pugmark was found on the jeep track near the stream crossing at 1330 hrs. Size suggests an adult male. Direction of travel was north. Followed the track for about 300 m but lost it on the rocky ground.

Patrol: vehicle patrol of 30 km to the northern boundary and back. No incidents.

Location: Base Camp
Weather: Clear, hot.

Morning meeting with the field team. Reviewed the snare incident from Tuesday. Decided to add a patrol route along the old logging road - we will check it every other day for the next two weeks.

Camera check at stations 2, 3, 4. All fine. Station 2 had a photo of a leopard at 2210 hrs - another clear shot. This is the same individual as before, I think. The spot pattern matches.

Field log entry: Suresh Patil reported elephant carcass on 2012-09-05. Record status: historical.

Time: 0745 hrs
Location: Base Camp
Weather: Clear, mild.

Station 9 had another bear photo at 0115 hrs - same individual as before, based on the chest marking. This is the fourth record of this bear in two weeks. It seems to be using the same trail regularly.

Time: 0800 hrs
Location: Base Camp

Time: 0745 hrs

4.2 Line Transect Sampling

In addition to the block counts, 22 line transects of 2 km length each were laid across different vegetation types, including dry deciduous forest, moist deciduous forest, scrubland, and riparian zones. Each transect was walked twice – once in the morning and once in the evening – over a three-day period (12/05/2012 to 14/05/2012). Perpendicular distances were recorded for all direct sightings, and the data were analysed using DISTANCE software (version 6.0) to estimate detection probabilities and density.

The transect data were used primarily to correct for under-detection in the block counts, especially for species with cryptic behaviour such as the Indian hare and the porcupine. For larger, more visible species like the elephant and the gaur, the block count figures were considered reliable without correction.

4.3 Data Compilation and Validation

Following the field exercise, all datasheets were compiled at the Divisional Forest Office in Chamarajanagar. Data entry was performed by two independent clerks, and discrepancies were resolved by referring to the original field sheets. A validation workshop was held on 20/05/2012 with the participation of range officers, the Deputy Conservator of Forests, and external researchers from the Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment (ATREE). During this workshop, the final estimates were reviewed against the previous year's figures and any anomalies were flagged.

The estimates presented in Tables 1 and 2 of this report are the outcome of this validation process. Where camera trap data were available, these were given greater weight for carnivore species. For ungulate species, the block count figures were accepted where the coefficient of variation was below 15%; where it exceeded this threshold, the transect-based estimates were used instead.

**WGCI Board Meeting Minutes**

**Date:** 19 October 2013
**Venue:** WGCI Head Office, Nagpur
**Time:** 10:30 AM to 1:45 PM

**Absent:**
- Dr. N. Bose (Board Member) – intimated leave

---

**Agenda Item 1: Confirmation of Minutes of Previous Meeting**

The minutes of the Board meeting held on 15 July 2013 were circulated to all members prior to the meeting. It was resolved that the minutes be confirmed as a true and accurate record of the proceedings. The Chairman signed the minutes.

---

**Agenda Item 2: Report on the Monsoon Camera Trap Survey – Nagzira-Navegaon Corridor**

Ms. L. D'Souza presented a summary of the camera trap survey conducted during August-September 2013. A total of 42 camera trap stations were deployed across the corridor, covering an area of approximately 180 sq. km. The survey recorded 14 individual tigers (including 3 cubs) and 31 individual leopards. Notably, the presence of a breeding female tiger in the central corridor was confirmed for the second consecutive year, indicating the functional connectivity of the habitat.

Ms. D'Souza also reported that the camera traps recorded an unusually high number of domestic cattle and goats, suggesting increased livestock pressure in the corridor. She recommended that the village liaison programme be strengthened to address this issue. The Board noted the report with appreciation and requested that a detailed scientific note be prepared for sharing with the State Forest Department.

---

**Agenda Item 3: Update on Village Forest Protection Committees**

Mr. K. V. Menon provided an update on the formation of village forest protection committees (VFPCs) in the villages surrounding the Nagzira-Navegaon corridor. As of 30 September 2013, 12 VFPCs have been formally constituted, with a total membership of 214 villagers. An additional 5 villages have expressed interest and are in the process of forming committees.

Mr. Menon highlighted that the VFPCs in the eastern part of the corridor have been particularly active, conducting regular patrolling and reporting two instances of illegal tree felling to the forest department. He noted that the success of the programme is dependent on the continued availability of small grants for community infrastructure projects, such as solar lighting and cattle proof trenches.

The Board resolved that the Community Engagement budget for the current financial year be reviewed in January 2014 to assess whether additional funds can be allocated to support the expansion of the VFPC programme.

---

**Agenda Item 4: Financial Report – Half Yearly (April to September 2013)**

Ms. P. Rao presented the statement of income and expenditure for the period 1 April 2013 to 30 September 2013. The total expenditure during the period was INR 68,40,000 against a revised annual budget of INR 1,48,50,000. The major items of expenditure were:

| Head | Expenditure (INR) |
|------|-------------------|
| Field Operations | 21,30,000 |
| Research & Monitoring | 12,80,000 |
| Community Engagement | 8,90,000 |
| Staff Salaries | 18,60,000 |
| Equipment & Supplies | 4,20,000 |
| Administrative Overheads | 2,60,000 |

Ms. Rao noted that expenditure under Field Operations was lower than anticipated during the monsoon months due to restricted vehicular movement. She proposed that the unspent amount be carried forward for the winter season, when intensive field work and the annual waterhole census would be undertaken. The Board approved the proposal.

Mr. Menon presented the field operations plan for the winter months (December 2013 to February 2014). The plan includes:

1. Annual waterhole census across the Nagzira-Navegaon corridor, scheduled for the second week of January.
2. Camera trap deployment in the central zone for a period of six weeks.
3. Anti-poaching patrols, with special emphasis on the northern fringe where movement of domestic cattle has increased.
4. Repair and maintenance of 14 km of internal patrol roads.

The total estimated cost for the winter operations is INR 9,80,000, which will be met from the unspent Field Operations allocation carried forward as approved in the half-yearly financial review.

**Agenda Item 3: Update on the Proposed Eco-Development Zone**

Mr. Menon reported on the ongoing consultations with the State Forest Department regarding the notification of an eco-development zone around the reserve. Three rounds of discussions have been held with the Deputy Conservator of Forests. The department has requested additional data on the habitat use patterns of wild dogs and sloth bears in the fringe areas.

Dr. Deshpande suggested that the Research & Monitoring team compile the available data from the last two years and submit it to the department by 15 January 2014. The Board agreed.

It was further noted that the boundaries proposed by the department differ from those suggested by WGCI in the eastern sector. A joint site visit has been proposed for the last week of January.

The Board noted that the Village Forest Protection Committees (VFPCs) have requested training on the use of GPS devices for patrolling. documents.title: Karnataka Forest Department Census Report
documents.content:
b) Waterhole Count: In addition to the block transects, waterhole counts were conducted at 22 permanent waterholes and 9 seasonal waterholes that still held water during the census period. Observers were positioned at each waterhole from 0600 hrs to 0900 hrs and from 1600 hrs to 1900 hrs on two consecutive days.

c) Pugmark Imprint Method: For carnivore species, pugmark imprints were collected on 15 designated pugmark pads located along animal trails and near water sources. Imprints were measured, photographed, and cross-verified by the WII team.

d) Camera Trap Exercise: A supplementary camera trap exercise was conducted in the months of March and April 2012, covering 40 trap locations in the core zone. The images were analyzed by the WII team and used to corroborate the pugmark data for tigers and leopards.

All data were recorded on standard census data sheets provided by the Wildlife Division, Chamarajanagara Circle. Data compilation was done at the Range level and subsequently consolidated at the Division level.

The increase is attributed to improved detection methods rather than an actual population growth, as the camera trap exercise identified 9 individual tigers through stripe pattern analysis, with 3 additional individuals detected only through pugmark evidence.

The final tiger estimate of 12 individuals is considered as the current official figure for the reserve as of May 2012 and will be reported to the NTCA for the All India Tiger Estimation exercise scheduled for 2014. 4.2 Line Transect Sampling

In addition to the block counts, 22 line transects of 2 km length each were laid across different vegetation types, including dry deciduous forest, moist deciduous forest, scrubland, and riparian zones. Each transect was walked twice – once in the morning and once in the evening – over a three-day period (12/05/2012 to 14/05/2012). Perpendicular distances were recorded for all direct sightings, and the data were analysed using DISTANCE software (version 6.0) to estimate detection probabilities and density.

The transect data were used primarily to correct for under-detection in the block counts, especially for species with cryptic behaviour such as the Indian hare and the porcupine. For larger, more visible species like the elephant and the gaur, the block count figures were considered reliable without correction.

4.3 Data Compilation and Validation

Following the field exercise, all datasheets were compiled at the Divisional Forest Office in Chamarajanagar. Data entry was performed by two independent clerks, and discrepancies were resolved by referring to the original field sheets. A validation workshop was held on 20/05/2012 with the participation of range officers, the Deputy Conservator of Forests, and external researchers from the Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment (ATREE). During this workshop, the final estimates were reviewed against the previous year's figures and any anomalies were flagged.

The estimates presented in Tables 1 and 2 of this report are the outcome of this validation process. Where camera trap data were available, these were given greater weight for carnivore species. For ungulate species, the block count figures were accepted where the coefficient of variation was below 15%; where it exceeded this threshold, the transect-based estimates were used instead.

Census report: elephant population estimate for Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve is 2500 individuals. Record status: current.

5. Regional Context and Comparison

The census was not limited to the Biligiri Rangaswamy Temple (BRT) Tiger Reserve. As part of the synchronised enumeration, the Karnataka Forest Department also conducted counts in the adjoining reserved forests and in the contiguous areas of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (NBR) that fall within Karnataka's jurisdiction. The NBR, which spans the states of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala, is one of the largest contiguous elephant habitats in India, and the data collected from the Karnataka portion are shared with the other states for the purpose of the regional population estimate.

6. Elephant Population Estimation for Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve

The elephant population estimate for Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve is 2500 individuals. This figure is the current official estimate, derived from the synchronised block count of May 2012 and validated through the dung-count calibration exercise. It supersedes the provisional figure of 2,380 individuals that was communicated to the State Wildlife Board in March 2012, which was based on a partial count covering only the eastern ranges.
